\chapter{Joining Words}
\label{ch:ka-joining}
\hlchaptermodality{64}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can join one Kannada answer to the next five ways, from afterwards to in that case.}

Complete KA-C64-in-that-case and say all five words in order.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[āmēle]{\kn{ಆಮೇಲೆ} (āmēle) — afterwards, later}

\label{lesson:KA-C64-after}



\begin{quote}
Before the new run: what did \emph{nōvu} mean, and what did \emph{ārōgya} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಆಮೇಲೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಆಮೇಲೆ}} (\emph{āmēle}) — \textquotedblleft{}afterwards, later\textquotedblright{}.

\kn{ಆಮೇಲೆ} opens with the same far-pointing \kn{ಆ} that stands at the front of \kn{ಅದು} and \kn{ಅಲ್ಲಿ}. Not this one, not here — that one, over there, and here it is time rather than place: not now, later.

Put it in front of a farewell you already own and you have a new one. \kn{ಆಮೇಲೆ} \kn{ಸಿಗೋಣ} sits beside \kn{ಮತ್ತೆ} \kn{ಸಿಗೋಣ} and \kn{ನಾಳೆ} \kn{ಸಿಗೋಣ}, three ways of promising the same thing with different amounts of commitment.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The first of five words that join one thing to the next.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{āmēle}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{āmēle}, then \emph{matte sigōṇa}, and say which one leaves the time open
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಆಮೇಲೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}afterwards, later\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kūḍa]{\kn{ಕೂಡ} (kūḍa) — also, too}

\label{lesson:KA-C64-also}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{āmēle} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಕೂಡ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಕೂಡ}} (\emph{kūḍa}) — \textquotedblleft{}also, too\textquotedblright{}.

\kn{ಕೂಡ} goes after the word it adds, not in front of it: \kn{ನಾನು} \kn{ಕೂಡ}, me as well. English puts \emph{also} almost anywhere in a sentence; Kannada puts this one straight behind the thing it is including and leaves it there.

The same shape carries the idea of coming together, which is where the adding sense comes from — two things joined, and the second one mentioned.

Take care with the middle letter. \kn{ಕೂಡ} and \kn{ಕೂದಲು} from the body chapter open alike and then part company, and in a rough spelling they can look closer than they are.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Two.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{kūḍa}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{nānu}, then \emph{nānu kūḍa}, and say which one adds somebody
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಕೂಡ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}also, too\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[innū]{\kn{ಇನ್ನೂ} (innū) — still, yet}

\label{lesson:KA-C64-still}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{kūḍa} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಇನ್ನೂ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಇನ್ನೂ}} (\emph{innū}) — \textquotedblleft{}still, yet\textquotedblright{}.

\kn{ಇನ್ನೂ} is the word for a thing that has not stopped or has not started. With \kn{ಇಲ್ಲ} behind it you get \emph{not yet}, which is the single most useful thing in this chapter.

It stacks with the measuring words from the replies chapter. \kn{ಇನ್ನೂ} \kn{ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ} is a little more still; \kn{ಇನ್ನೂ} \kn{ಹೆಚ್ಚು} is more than that again. One word in front and your five replies have doubled.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Three.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{innū}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{svalpa}, then \emph{innū svalpa}, and say which one asks for more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಇನ್ನೂ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}still, yet\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bēga]{\kn{ಬೇಗ} (bēga) — soon, quickly}

\label{lesson:KA-C64-soon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{innū} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಬೇಗ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಬೇಗ}} (\emph{bēga}) — \textquotedblleft{}soon, quickly\textquotedblright{}.

\kn{ಬೇಗ} is inherited, and it holds hurry and nearness-in-time on one shape. \kn{ಬೇಗ} \kn{ಬಾ} is \emph{come quickly} and equally \emph{come soon}, and which one is meant is settled by everything around it rather than by the word.

Set it against \emph{īga}, the now-word from the leave-taking chapter. \emph{Īga} is this moment. \kn{ಬೇಗ} is a moment that has not arrived but will not keep you waiting. They rhyme and are unrelated, which by now should surprise you less than it did.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Four.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{bēga}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{īga}, then \emph{bēga}, and say which one has not happened yet
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಬೇಗ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}soon, quickly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[hāgādare]{\kn{ಹಾಗಾದರೆ} (hāgādare) — in that case, then}

\label{lesson:KA-C64-in-that-case}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{bēga} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಹಾಗಾದರೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಹಾಗಾದರೆ}} (\emph{hāgādare}) — \textquotedblleft{}in that case, then\textquotedblright{}.

\kn{ಹಾಗಾದರೆ} is built out of \kn{ಹಾಗೆ}, the \emph{that way} word from the earlier replies chapter, with an \emph{if it becomes} wrapped around it. If it is that way — in that case.

It is the word that lets you answer a fact with a decision. Somebody says the shop is shut; you say \kn{ಹಾಗಾದರೆ} \kn{ಆಮೇಲೆ}, and with two of this chapter's five words you have made a plan without a single naming-word in it.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Five: \kn{ಆಮೇಲೆ}, \kn{ಕೂಡ}, \kn{ಇನ್ನೂ}, \kn{ಬೇಗ}, \kn{ಹಾಗಾದರೆ}. Enough to keep a conversation moving without answering yes or no.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{hāgādare}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item all five in order, then \emph{hāge}, then \emph{hāgādare}, and say which came from which
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಹಾಗಾದರೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}in that case, then\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
